building: Lawson Hall / Richard and Patricia Lawson Computer Science Building

changes.action: Re-registered plan-derived room/stair/interior objects using three matched wall corners shared by the Purdue north-up L1 raster and the GIS FID 59 polygon. Recovered separate X/Y scale factors of 0.092105 and 0.09233778 m/pixel.
changes.evidence: Control pairs: PDF pixels (323,86), (627,86), (298,986) to project-local GIS coordinates (-13.209,40.611), (14.791,40.547), (-15.553,-42.493). PDF scale bar independently reads approximately 0.092 m/pixel.
changes.limits: Raster wall-edge picks and line thickness give about 0.3 m registration uncertainty. This is an axis-aligned image fit, not a survey; no facade elevation was inferred.

changes.feature: Fresh GIS-to-shell comparison and footprint corrections
changes.action: Compared all 54 ordered vertices/edges in official GIS FID 59 against the lower structural wall lines in the saved Blender source. Restored the full southeast vestibule boundary using GIS vertices 42-52 without diagonal shortcuts and added a 3.965 m north-edge closure matching GIS edge 6->7.
changes.evidence: A fresh lower-baseline comparison samples each of the 54 GIS boundary edges at 21 points (1,134 total). Before R7 additions, 83.95% were within 0.10 m; after the vestibule and north closure, 100% were within 0.10 m, with a maximum nearest-line distance of 0.000015 m. The live EPSG:4326 FID 59 snapshot and project polygon agree to a maximum 0.000636 m after the documented project tangent-plane conversion; project polygon values are rounded to millimeters.
changes.limits: The check measures XY lower wall-line alignment only; it does not verify wall thickness, all above-grade surfaces, elevations, or the correctness of the GIS source itself. The north closure follows the source in plan; its 14.55 m vertical extent copies the neighboring schematic exterior wall and remains unverified. No window cadence was inferred on that edge.

changes.action: Rebuilt wall panels along the ordered GIS vestibule perimeter. Limited the photo-guided limestone canopy to the principal GIS/plan entrance wall instead of wrapping the whole vestibule. Added illustrative paired door framing, sign, treads and three handrail runs.
changes.evidence: Purdue L1 plan and FID 59 support location and horizontal shell perimeter. Purdue-published 2024 entrance image supports limestone canopy, named fascia, doors, steps and metal rails.
changes.limits: Vestibule wall top at 3.55 m, canopy top at 3.78 m, canopy 1.20 m projection/0.70 m side extensions/0.40 m convex bow, door opening width, mullions, sign dimensions, stair/rail sizes are visual estimates; no measured elevation or entrance detail was found.

changes.action: Checked Purdue CS first-floor plan, official construction/entrance photography, the Purdue Archives UA 113 public collection description, and Purdue GIS attributes for elevation/upper-floor evidence.
changes.evidence: The public GIS record reports NUM_LEVELS=5 but its Extrution and other dimensional-looking fields do not document units or a measurement method. Purdue Archives UA 113 describes one folder with an information booklet and blank greeting cards, not a drawing set. Purdue CS construction article describes brickwork and window installation but supplies no measured elevation.
changes.limits: No public measured/current roof elevation, complete upper-floor floor plans, or verified floor-to-floor stair section was found. Roof, penthouse/equipment heights and facade opening cadence remain schematic/unverified; no roof geometry was changed.

changes.action: Reopened the saved asset independently for refreshed exterior, first-floor cutaway, vestibule close-up, and 16-panel Commons-wall views.
changes.evidence: The images are `exterior_round7.png`, `interior_cutaway_round7.png`, `entry_lobby_round7.png`, and `commons_wall_round7.png` in this audit folder.
changes.limits: Temporary cameras, lights, render visibility flags, cutaway floor material and staging are not saved into the building asset.

changes.feature: Official second- and third-floor plans, registered to GIS
changes.action: Downloaded Purdue CS LWSN second-floor and third-floor plan PDFs, rasterized at 120 dpi, registered them to the R7 north-up L1/GIS affine using the same wall-control points after 10/9 pixel rescaling, and compared the GIS ring to source outline strokes. Added GIS footprint slabs and plan-traced schematic L2/L3 partition walls (75 and 87 retained long orthogonal source segments).
changes.evidence: Official source pages: lawson_2.PDF and lawson_3.PDF. Red GIS overlays are gis_plan_overlay_l2_round8.png and gis_plan_overlay_l3_round8.png. Nearest teal perimeter stroke: L2 975/1,113 samples recognized, mean 0.121 m, max 0.725 m; 905/975 recognized within 0.30 m. L3 1,027/1,113 recognized, mean 0.106 m, max 0.670 m; 950/1,027 within 0.30 m. Three-control transform is 0.0828945 X and 0.0831040 Y m/pixel; see upper_plan_registration_round8.json.
changes.limits: The floor sheets are raster images and the source stroke is not survey linework; max offsets indicate local plan/GIS envelope differences and/or line-pick limits. Raster extraction captures long orthogonal partition lines, not every wall/door. Story Z, partition thickness (0.12 m), height (2.55 m), and furniture are schematic and unmeasured. L2/L3 plan stair symbols and directions are documented, but no continuous 3D stair flights or section are claimed.

changes.feature: Third-floor Tolonga Terrace and roof footprint
changes.action: Used the official L3 plan label Tolonga Terrace and Purdue CS Building Hours listing for a 3rd-floor terrace/balcony to notch the roof deck across the source-drawn terrace zone. The exterior ring follows GIS FID 59; the terrace inner edge is traced from the registered L3 plan. The R8 roof remains at the previous model datum of 13.8 m, unverified.
changes.evidence: Purdue LWSN third-floor PDF and Lawson Building Hours source. R8 exterior preview and reopened roof mesh are included in evidence.
changes.limits: The terrace plan boundary trace has about 0.3 m raster pick/registration uncertainty. Roof elevation and terrace guard/rail detail are not established by the plan.

changes.action: Reduced the long, bulky penthouse and equipment group to proportions closer to Purdue's 2006 exterior/aerial photos. The penthouse now measures 8.5 x 20.0 x 3.8 m, rooftop equipment group 8 x 14 x 1.4 m, with overall model maximum Z=19.0 m.
changes.evidence: Purdue CS March 2006 building update image and official dedication aerial/exterior photograph; raw local copies are listed below. Geometry details are recorded in roof_photo_refinement_round8.json.
changes.limits: Perspective photos support only relative silhouette. Resized values and all roof/penthouse/equipment heights remain visual estimates; no dimensioned roof/elevation drawing was found.

remaining_uncertainty: No dimensioned/current roof or whole-building elevation was found. The main roof datum (13.8 m), maximum Z (19.0 m), penthouse size and equipment dimensions remain visually estimated, not measured.
Purdue GIS reports NUM_LEVELS=5 but does not document the height field's units/measurement method. Upper L2/L3 floor Z values (4.0 and 7.2 m) and partition dimensions remain schematic.

Official L1/L2/L3 plans show stair symbols and UP/DOWN directions, but no section or complete fourth-floor/basement plans verified continuous stair route; upper stair flights are intentionally not fabricated.
The second/third floor partition traces are long orthogonal centerlines from raster plans. Smaller partitions, door openings, wall thickness, furniture, and room heights remain illustrative.
The L3 plan labels Tolonga Terrace and official building hours confirm a 3rd-floor terrace/balcony. The roof notch follows its plan footprint; no measured terrace rail detail or elevation found.

GIS-to-floorplan outline samples show local differences up to 0.725 m (L2) and 0.670 m (L3) among recognized perimeter strokes; plan/GIS raster overlay remains approximate, with about 0.3 m control-pick uncertainty.
Exterior window cadence beyond visible photos and material/glazing specifications remain visual; the 2006 facade photos are historical perspective references.
